title: From Collapse to Control: Understanding and Extending Context Length in Emerging Hybrid Models via Universal Position Interpolation
claim: Hybrid models collapse beyond their training context length, and naive position scaling does not fix the failure.
layout: 1 panel, dual y-axes, solid vs dashed lines, left-to-right context-length axis
description: A single line plot with a shared x-axis of context length in tokens, from 2048 to 32768. The left y-axis is blue and shows perplexity from 0 to 25. The right y-axis is red and shows retrieval accuracy in percent from 0 to 100. Blue lines with circle markers show perplexity. It stays near 8–9 up to 8K, then rises sharply past 16K and goes off the chart. Red lines with x markers show accuracy. It starts at about 100% at 2K–4K, drops to about 40% at 8K, and falls to near 0 at 32K. Solid lines are Bamba v2 and dashed lines are Bamba v2 with YaRN. The two versions track each other closely, so YaRN gives little help. A legend sits at lower left. The eye goes first to the crossing blue and red curves around 8K.
caption: Performance of state-of-the-art hybrid model on long-context tasks. Blue lines denote perplexity(↓) on PG-19 validation set; red lines show retrieval accuracy(↑) on Needle-in-a-Haystack Single-Key-2 task from RULER (Hsieh et al., 2024a). Model: Bamba v2 (Ganti et al.), with 4k training context. YaRN applied without tuning.
abstract: Hybrid Mamba-Transformer models have emerged as promising alternatives to pure Transformers, offering efficiency and competitive performance. However, they struggle to generalize beyond their training context windows, collapsing on long-context tasks. We provide the first systematic analysis of this failure, showing that it arises from uncontrolled state growth and uneven receptive field contributions across the hybrid architecture. Guided by this understanding, we introduce Universal Position Interpolation (UPI), a closed-form, training-free scaling method that unifies Mamba's cumulative decay with Transformer rotary frequency scaling. UPI selectively stabilizes unstable Mamba dynamics while rescaling Transformer encodings, controlling state growth and enabling reliable long-context generalization, with only a few auxiliary forward passes. Evaluation shows that UPI extends multiple state-of-the-art hybrid and pure Mamba models from 4K to up to 64K tokens on PG-19 perplexity, LongBench and RULER benchmarks, without sacrificing short-context accuracy. These findings establish the first principled bridge between Transformers and state-space models and open a new direction for training-free context extension methods for emerging hybrid models.
